doc.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018

title: Charice's career, his wife, and his devotion to her
summary: Charice's Ellen show, David Foster deal and coming out, alongside his marriage to his wife.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Ellen show. And Ellen said, “Everybody get out your handkerchiefs.” And she was moved. She’s like five foot one, ninety-one pounds, and she sang and she got a standing ovation. She came over with her mother, from the Philippines. And she was crying after she finished, because she got a standing ovation. She had a very rough life. A year later she got a thirteen million dollar deal through David Foster who is the Hit Man, he’s got fifteen gold records. And he had heard of her. He became her stepfather. She toured. And that’s the last person on the tour with famous people from Earth, Wind & Fire — anybody you can name, to see this little girl. But I watched her for three years, two or three hours at a time at nighttime, crying seventy percent of the time. I was going — I’ve had a lot of dreams — I just believe we’ve been together in another lifetime. I’ve had past lives. A lot of people don’t believe in that. She is like a sweetheart to me. It’s not romantic at all, I just have a deep love and joy that’s unsurpassed. And I’m almost crying now. It’s something like — I don’t have any kids. If you had a 5-year-old sweetie. My wife is my sweetheart. I met her in a dream, had a romantic dream with her two months before I went to Japan. And I met her. And she’s been my sweetheart for thirty-three years. And I thank God almost every day to be with her. I’ve hardly ever had a hassle with her. She’s a real — I’ve never met a real sweetheart. I’ve had girlfriends, I’ve been married before, she’s just that sweet. But this girl is very humble, she can sing like an angel, I heard she breaks microphones when she sings, that powerful. She said, “What you hear is my mom. Everything you see if my mother.” My mom is like, I want to be like the best daughter to my mom. And then last year she came out, a couple of years ago, she came out, she just had a sex operation and she changed. Because when she was thirteen, she told Oprah, she was on the Oprah show eight times. Oprah said, “You’re the most talented girl in the world.” It’s crazy. Eight times in one year. And she told Oprah in an interview in an interview two years ago, she said, “Are you a lesbian?” She said, “Yeah.” She said, “When I was thirteen I didn’t tell my mom but I had some relationship.” But when she was seen with David Foster, at fifteen or sixteen, in front of eighteen thousand people with Celine had her sing at Madison Square Garden, she got a standing ovation. Celine said, “She sings better than me” on the Oprah show the next week. Oprah said, “Weren’t you afraid she is going to miss a note?” She said, “No. I knew she was going to sing better than me.” I’m crying you know. So it goes on. It’s just incredible — I wrote to her. It took me three hours to write a letter to her. And I’ve had a lot of beautiful twenty year old girls. My wife is my sweetheart. But she is like a sweetheart. She never brags about herself and she just — but the thing that touched me watching her interview last year, besides saying she is gay, she said, “After I sang for eighteen thousand people and got a standing ovation” or something, “I go up to my room
and cry because I’m gay and no one knew. Like I wasn’t ready to tell people.” I mean it just breaks my heart.
